subject: Request: HeartCare enterprise package rate-floor exception
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Lee <emily@heartcare.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: HeartCare enterprise package rate-floor exception

Hi Emily — great to speak yesterday. Per our conversation I wanted to capture a formal commercial proposal so we can align expectations and, if needed, escalate for exec sign-off. High-level ask from HeartCare summarized here and our recommended routing.

Customer ask (from call)
- 35% off list on Dedicated GPU capacity in year 1
- Waived onboarding and first-month setup fees
- 2-year commitment with ramp to steady-state in month 6

Quick notes from our side (preliminary economics)
- Estimated Yr1 billings: ~$450k ARR if they hit forecasted usage (attached forecast)
- Unit economics: with 35% + waived onboarding we drop below our target contribution margin on dedicated configs; this is why we need an exception path

Recommended commercial exception for exec review
- Approve up to 30% off list (first 12 months)
- 2-year commitment with a minimum first-year ARR guarantee of $300k
- Waive onboarding but apply a 3-month rolling true-up for usage (to protect against over-provisioning)
- Require standard MSA + audit rights preserved

Attachments: HeartCare_MAPlan.xlsx (mutual action plan), usage_forecast.csv

Next steps: Emily, if this framing looks reasonable I'll loop in Marissa and request CFO sign-off. They indicated they need written confirmation by Apr 10 to make procurement cycles.

Thanks,
Monica
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Emily Lee <emily@heartcare.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@heartcare.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: HeartCare enterprise package rate-floor exception

Thanks Monica — appreciate the clear summary. We are definitely interested in Redwood for the Dedicated runbook (latency profile and KV caching are attractive). A couple clarifications from procurement:

- Our finance team is asking for 35% off list in year 1 to get budget approval across three business units.
- They also want the onboarding fee waived and an implementation milestone credit if rollout slips beyond M+3.
- Timeline: we need a signed commercial term sheet by Apr 10 to align with our Q2 board refresh.

If you can escalate and get a documented approval path (VP/CFO sign-off) we can move fast. I can provide a short statement of intent from our CFO if that helps.

Best,
Emily Lee
Head of Platform Partnerships | HeartCare AI
emily@heartcare.ai

On Thu, Mar 22, 2028 at 09:12 AM Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Emily — great to speak yesterday. Per our conversation I wanted to capture a formal commercial proposal so we can align expectations and, if needed, escalate for exec sign-off...
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Mar 2028 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: HeartCare commercial exception request — business case

Marissa / Markus — forwarding Emily's note. Procurement is pushing for 35% off list in year 1 plus onboarding waived; timeline is Apr 10. Summary and recommended path below.

Why this matters
- Strategic fit: HeartCare is a clinical-imaging workflow start-up with immediate production use-cases for our Dedicated offering; platform integration would be a strong reference for medtech verticals.
- ARR upside: forecasted spend is ~$450k ARR in year 1 if adoption goes to plan; potential upsell into embeddings and Rerank later.

Risk / economics
- At 35% + onboarding waive our contribution margin on Dedicated GPUs falls below threshold for sustained deployments.
- Our ask is to limit downside with a minimum ARR guarantee and a usage true-up.

My recommended exception for exec review
- Approve up to 30% discount first 12 months (not 35%)
- 2-year committed term, with first-year minimum ARR guarantee of $300k (true-up quarterly)
- Waive onboarding but include an implementation milestone credit (credit applied only if implementation > M+3)
- Require signed MSA and audit rights; no change to data residency or logging obligations

Attachments: HeartCare_MAPlan.xlsx, usage_forecast.csv

Can you advise if CFO sign-off is possible on this path? If approved I will prepare a redline term sheet and loop Legal + RevOps for DocuSign and revenue ops tagging.

Thanks,
Monica

> On Thu, Mar 22, 2028 at 11:05 AM Emily Lee <emily@heartcare.ai> wrote:
> > Thanks Monica — appreciate the clear summary...
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Mar 2028 12:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: HeartCare commercial exception request — business case

Markus / Monica — I’ve reviewed Monica’s recommendation. HeartCare is strategically worthwhile as a medtech reference and could accelerate similar deals in the sector. I'm comfortable with a tighter concession than their ask. Proposed commercial counter we should present to them (subject to your sign-off, Markus):

- Discount: 25% off list for first 12 months (not to exceed 27% without CFO approval)
- Year 2: standard published list (or limited 10% reduction if they commit to a usage threshold > $600k ARR)
- Minimum first-year ARR guarantee: $300k (quarterly true-ups, clawback if below threshold)
- Waive onboarding fee; provide a single implementation milestone credit (one-time) if rollout misses M+3 by 45+ days
- Require MSA + redlined term sheet; legal to confirm audit and liability language unchanged

Monica — please propose this counter to Emily today and note we’ll need CFO sign-off on anything above 25% or any revenue concessions beyond the minimum. I’ll prepare the redline term sheet (attaching draft).

Best,
Marissa Cole
VP, North America Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachment: redlined_term_sheet.pdf
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Legal <legal@redwood.ai>, RevOps <revops@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 24 Mar 2028 15:06:00 -0700
Subject: CFO sign-off: HeartCare rate-floor exception — conditional

Quick decision: conditional CFO approval granted. I will sign off on a commercial exception within the following limits and conditions. Please ensure RevOps and Legal execute before DocuSign.

CFO conditional approval (terms)
- Approved discount: up to 27% off list for year 1 (monitored at deal close)
- Requirement: signed 2-year commitment with minimum first-year ARR guarantee of $300k
- Payment cadence: upfront or quarterly prepay; no monthly net-30 in initial term without Finance approval
- Implementation credit: single milestone credit only (must be documented in the term sheet)
- Overages: bill at published overage rates; no further credits once first invoice is issued
- Audit & MSA: Legal must keep audit rights intact; no changes that increase indemnity exposure
- Revenue recognition: RevOps to put a hold flag until signed MSA + payment cadence confirmed

Operational asks:
- Monica: present the 27%/2-year package as Marissa suggested, mark that final approval requires signed MSA and prepayment cadence.
- Marissa: send the final redline to Legal and confirm the DocuSign envelope.
- RevOps: apply deal_id DL-HTC-2028-0322 and place a revenue recognition hold pending contract execution.

I will author a CFO approval memo for the deal folder once Legal confirms redlines; include this memo in the HubSpot deal.

Markus Klein
CFO | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai
